title: The Hundredth
protagonist: The Chief Judge (a role; a constructed decision point -- the real referee reviewed high-speed video and the result stood)
primary_metric: probability the ruling instrument names the swimmer whose hand reached the wall first, in a close finish

options.A: Pad Ranks -- the touchpad result orders the finish, as the rule is written
options.B: Contact Ranks -- first hand contact on high-speed video orders the finish

excluded_sources: A touchpad activation force of 3 kg appears in an Olympedia commentary (S1's page); other write-ups give different figures with no primary source. Not used.

The Olympedia commentary says Serbia's protest cited Omega's sponsorship of Phelps; ABC and Wikipedia report the protest as alleging Cavic touched first without enough force. The case attributes the allegation only to ABC's report and states the sources differ in the research log.
'Serbia accepted the footage' (reported in an NBC summary; no named primary statement found). Not used.
NBC's report that FINA reviewed timing 'to ten-thousandths' was not corroborated; not used.

Wording 'sliding while Phelps was pushing/rushing the pad' and 'big difference between touching and pushing', attributed to Omega's Berthaud in search snippets: a P6 fetch found it only in a reader comment on the Swimming World page. Not used.
scenario_constructions: The Chief Judge is a role, not a named person; the decision point (choosing which instrument orders the finish) is constructed. The real referee, Ben Ekumbo, reviewed footage and the result was upheld; FINA's ruling stands and the case never implies it was wrong.

The reliability rule P = 1 - b/(2W), the scenario values (delta 0.010 s, J 0.005 s, 240 fps, W 0.05 s) and the Twist (only a 60 fps feed shows the wall) are constructions for the discussion, not historical facts.
The scenario is built so that no dead heat is available: reported times differ and SW 11.2 awards a shared placing only to equal times at one hundredth. No shared gold.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The differential pad lag between the two lanes
modeling_assumptions.value: Swept from -0.010 s to 0.030 s; scenario value 0.010 s for D5
modeling_assumptions.basis: Plausible range, not measured. No published lag figure was found; no lag number is attributed to Omega or FINA. The named claims in Appendix A (stroking vs gliding; force on the pad) point in different directions.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value (student-facing wording; the size and direction are facilitator-only, see sensitivity_disclosure).

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Frame rate of the footage under review
modeling_assumptions.value: 240 fps scenario value; 30/60/240/1000 listed as examples
modeling_assumptions.basis: The frame rate of the footage reviewed in 2008 was not found in any source.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The judge's extra reading band J for calling first contact
modeling_assumptions.basis: No source gives a figure for how precisely a judge can call first contact from footage.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Definition of a close finish: true margin equally likely anywhere within +/-W
modeling_assumptions.basis: A definition for this model; not a measurement.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes the scale of the probabilities for both options in the same direction.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Average speed used for centimetre conversions near the wall
modeling_assumptions.basis: A stand-in; a stroking hand moves faster and a gliding hand slower near the wall.

sensitivity_note: Teacher-facing: real named people and a real protest -- keep the register neutral (race and protest only, no motive); FINA's ruling stands. The margin exists only for the scenario values and is fragile to a +/-50% change in any one of the lag, judge band or frame rate. Two contested first-contact claims (Ekumbo vs Bertaud) are attributed and never resolved. No SPEC section 6 harm subject (no death, illness or hardship).

balance.argument_a: Pad Ranks is objective, resolved far finer than the reported hundredths, applied identically to every race and fixed in advance by the rule as written. Its only weakness is a DIFFERENTIAL lag between lanes: a lag common to both cancels, so it matters only if it exceeds the reported gap. If that differential is small (the scenario value of 0.010 s gives a probability of 0.900, and any value below 0.00917 s beats the video), the pad is at least as reliable as footage whose frame period plus a human reading band is nearly as wide.
balance.argument_b: Contact Ranks measures what the sport is meant to reward, the swimmer's hand reaching the wall, rather than the pad's registration. At 240 fps one frame is 0.0042 s (0.82 cm), narrower than the 0.01 s gap, so with the scenario values its indecision band is 0.00917 s and its probability is 0.9083, ahead of the pad. Cost: a judge must still call first contact (J), and only frame rates above 100 fps can separate a hundredth.
balance.margin_basis: P = 1 - b/(2W); A: b = |delta| ; B: b = 1/fps + J; W = 0.05 s. Scenario values give A = 0.900, B = 0.9083.
balance.twist_effect: Only a 60 fps feed clearly shows the wall (a constructed what-if): frame period 0.01667 s, B band 0.02167 s, P_B = 0.7833 against P_A = 0.900; the winner flips to Pad Ranks by 14.9%. The twist states that the judge band J is unchanged and no sub-frame interpolation is allowed.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA1, no published lag figure exists for either swimmer. Flexing +50% (to 0.015 s) keeps Contact Ranks ahead (6.86%, within cap); flexing -50% (to 0.005 s) flips the winner to Pad Ranks (4.59%, within cap). The break-even is delta = 1/fps + J = 0.00917 s. A disclosed, not eliminated, instability: no research can tighten it short of measuring the pad.

MA3, no source quantifies how precisely a judge reads first contact from footage. +50% (to 0.0075 s) flips the winner to Pad Ranks (1.89%); -50% (to 0.0025 s) widens Contact Ranks' lead (3.70%). Within the 20% cap in both directions.

MA2, the frame rate of the 2008 review footage was not found. +50% (to 360 fps) widens Contact Ranks' lead (2.47%); -50% (to 120 fps) flips the winner to Pad Ranks (3.85%). Within the 20% cap in both directions. The twist (60 fps) pulls this same lever.

deliverables.text: Winner's average speed (m/s) from the race distance and time, and the distance in centimetres a hand travels in one hundredth of a second; one sentence on why it is only an approximation.
A frame-rate band table: time between frames and hand travel per frame for each frame rate in Appendix D; which rates can separate a one-hundredth difference.
The smallest and largest true pad-time difference consistent with reported 50.58 and 50.59 if the third digit is dropped versus rounded, in seconds and centimetres.
A completed differential-lag table (implied first-contact margin and who touched first), the student's own plausible range for the lag, defended using named claims as claims, and the threshold value.
Each option's indecision band, probability of ordering a close finish correctly, and the percent difference, with the scenario values and with the student's own range.
A written 'what the model leaves out' section naming at least three simplifications, the one that most threatens the recommendation, and a measurement that would settle it.

facilitator.twist: The fast camera's view of the wall was blocked by spray; the only angle clearly showing both hands is a 60 fps feed. The judge reading band J is unchanged and nobody may interpolate between frames. Flips the winner to Pad Ranks.

concepts: Reading a reported time as a range
catalog.ask: A one-hundredth-of-a-second margin, a touchpad and a camera: which instrument should get the last word when they could disagree, and how big would the pad's hidden difference between lanes have to be?

context_glossary.desc: The international federation that governs swimming and other water sports and wrote the swimming rules this case quotes. It has since been renamed World Aquatics.
A swimming stroke in which both arms sweep together over the water and the legs kick together. The race in this case is a 100 m butterfly.
A tie in a race: the performances are judged so close that no difference can be resolved, so the competitors share a placing.
How many still images a video records or shows each second, measured in frames per second. Anything that happens between two frames cannot be seen exactly.
